newsitem.title: CHINA: China Telecom sees more links with HK Telecom.
newsitem.headline: China Telecom sees more links with HK Telecom.

text.p: China Telecom (Hong Kong) Ltd said on Thursday it foresees increased cooperation with Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd, in which it holds a 5.5 percent stake.

"The formation of China Telecom (Hong Kong) and all the actions and measures it has taken...are principally aimed at promoting the long-term stability and prosperity of Hong Kong and the cooperation in the telecommunications sector between Hong Kong and mainland China," China Telecom (Hong Kong) vice chairman and general manager Chen Zhaobin said in a statement.
This would "undoubtedly further promote long-term cooperation between China Telecom and Hongkong Telecom" and would help Hongkong Telecom's long-term business development, Chen said.
"This will also be beneficial to China Telecom's effort to further develop its international cooperation," Chen said.

China Telecom (Hong Kong), controlled by Telpo Communications Ltd, an arm of China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (MPT), last month agreed to pay US$1.185 billion to buy a 5.5 percent stake in Hongkong Telecom from Cable & Wireless Plc (C&W).
Hongkong Telecom chairman Brian Smith said earlier this month that China Telecom (Hong Kong) had indicated it might buy more of Hongkong Telecom in coming months.
Chen's statement was issued one day after a signing ceremony at which 19 banks agreed to lend a China Telecom (Hong Kong) arm US$860 million to part-finance the US$1.185 billion purchase.
China Telecom (Hong Kong) will use its Hongkong Telecom shares as security for the loan.
A Hong Kong newspaper reported that the restructuring of China Telecom (Hong Kong) ahead of its proposed listing in Hong Kong had received official approval in China.

The Hong Kong Standard quoted a China Telecom (Hong Kong) executive as saying China's Securities Regulatory Commission had approved the injection of some mainland cellular phone operations into China Telecom (Hong Kong).
The listing is expected in the fourth quarter of the year.
